signal_or_failure: A Brooks cable with tinsel braid proved 'so defective from the start' that no more than 15 wires were ever connected through it
what_it_demonstrated: that a named supplier's product was written off while the engineers were still discussing it
what_it_did_not_demonstrate: that the loss was priced anywhere - no dollar figure is printed
notes: an incurred engineering failure recorded in the survivor's own house print, which is why it survives

signal_or_failure: Lead-sheath corrosion: 600 feet drawn out for defective insulation and replaced; the replacement also corroding
magnitude: about 9,400 feet still in service under active corrosion
what_it_demonstrated: that material choice (pure lead vs lead-tin) was a live failure variable
what_it_did_not_demonstrate: the eventual cost of the programme; the report notes the corrosion continuing 'until the lead is destroyed'
notes: Western Electric's tin-hardened sheath showed 'scarcely any signs of decay' in the same test set

signal_or_failure: Boston conduit cables failed: the Phillips cable gave out September 1884 and two Clark cables in March 1885 on defective insulation; the Phillips cable was not removed until February 1887 and its covering was 'badly rotted'
magnitude: six cables placed in 1883; two classes of failure
what_it_demonstrated: that failures were reported across companies within a day of the request for information
what_it_did_not_demonstrate: whether the loss was charged anywhere; no figure is printed
evidence_class: CONTEMPORANEOUS (a third company's letter inside P2's print)
notes: the only held cross-company failure record in the window; also the source of the 1853-for-1883 OCR defect at U.5

signal_or_failure: The longest Boston cable, 1,500 feet, did not carry conversation beyond the suburbs
what_it_demonstrated: that early underground plant had a hard physical ceiling
what_it_did_not_demonstrate: that the company knew the cause in 1883 - the account is told in 1914
notes: pairs with the 1881 'small results' experiment: two failures before the twisted pair

signal_or_failure: The Chicago & Milwaukee Telegraph Line went into receivership and was sold in 1907 to the Chicago and Wisconsin Telephone Companies in connection with the registrant
magnitude: stock of 50,000, then 50,000 of stock and 50,000 of bonds; 27 years from speculation to sale
what_it_demonstrated: the corpus's first incurred commercial failure, and the registrant's first documented absorption of a toll line
what_it_did_not_demonstrate: anything about P4 - it did not exist; and the appendix reprint is a polemic, not a company statement
evidence_class: FACT (reprint inside the registrant's own print)
notes: U.8: the only incorporation-with-capital figure in held non-SEC bytes belongs to THIS failed company, not to P2

signal_or_failure: The registrant consented to receivers over the Central Union Telephone Company's Chicago property rather than adjust on terms
magnitude: territory covering most of Ohio and Indiana and part of Illinois
what_it_demonstrated: that a competitor's network was being taken apart with the registrant's acquiescence
what_it_did_not_demonstrate: that the registrant benefited: the report says adjustment on any reasonable basis was impossible
notes: corroborated in kind by the 1908 pamphlet's quotation of Central Union's own 1907 plea for rate relief

signal_or_failure: System surplus earnings fell to 11,735,194 from 13,221,110 and the balance of net profits fell 644,426, while gross rose 16,400,668
magnitude: as printed in the comparison of 1912 and 1913
what_it_demonstrated: that growth was being consumed: 14.6M of a 16.4M gross increase went to expenses
what_it_did_not_demonstrate: a cause: no held byte attributes the squeeze to competition, regulation or cost error
notes: the negative signal that keeps the 1913 print from reading as a success story

signal_or_failure: The independent wave's own collapse, printed by one of its managers: companies asking for increased rates and absolution from conditions 'freely accepted and assumed at the beginning'; reorganizations in progress
what_it_demonstrated: that competition's failure rate was being admitted inside the competing movement
what_it_did_not_demonstrate: that the Bell System was therefore vindicated - the pamphlet's author immediately argues the opposite from Bell's own behaviour
notes: a two-sided null: neither network was demonstrably healthy from held bytes

signal_or_failure: Loud-speaking telephone promotions: the company states that misunderstanding of loss caused 'loss to many who have invested'
what_it_demonstrated: that a competing technical route failed, in the registrant's telling
what_it_did_not_demonstrate: any independent confirmation of the losses; the source is self-serving
confidence: Medium (that it was printed) UNKNOWN (the losses)
notes: no investor, amount or company is named

signal_or_failure: Wholesale obsolescence asserted: the twisted pair 'meant the abandonment of the entire underground plant of the Bell System'
what_it_demonstrated: that the firm's own account treats its installed base as perishable
what_it_did_not_demonstrate: the magnitude: the dossier refuses to convert this into an impairment number
